stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Harness changes for the INV dimension (procedure/tool-use/completion only; no subject-matter or deliverable-shape changes). All citations are to the sole trajectory, context/rollouts/base1.md.

1. scripts/extract_sources.py (NEW — shipped in the proposal)
   One-pass deterministic extraction of every file in documents/ to named plain-text files under extract/ (docx/xlsx/pptx/pdf via the runtime's read_doc.py --in host; .eml decoded via the stdlib email module; manifest printed; per-file failure tolerance).
   Motivating moments:
   - base1.md:21-59 — plain `python3 scripts/read_doc.py <doc>` failed twice with FileNotFoundError('podman') (blind repetition) before the agent read the script source and discovered `--in host`. The script bakes in the working invocation.
   - base1.md:547, 1194, 2216 — every large extraction overflowed into anonymous .ocdata/opencode/tool-output/tool_<id> cache files, which then required ~13 paged re-reads (1066, 2294, 2611, 2819, 3046, 3228, 3486, 3837, 3905) and had to be manually re-recorded in both compaction summaries (2438-2441, 4845-4848, 5488-5491). Named extracts under extract/ survive compaction and are greppable.
   - base1.md:3962, 4710, 5295 — three different hand-rolled python email one-liners to decode the quoted-printable .eml (slices [:9000], [9000:20000], then a full part-walk). One decoder, run once.
   - base1.md:5041-5366 — the late switch to rg-over-cached-text was the only efficient citation pattern in the run; the script makes that the default from the start.

2. tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md (was empty — filled)
   Workspace facts, labelled as verified: read_doc.py requires `--in host` (podman absent) plus a stop condition if host mode itself fails; .eml files are quoted-printable (raw read shows =E2=80=94 escapes); read caps at ~50KB/2000 lines and bash overflow lands in anonymous cache files; run extract_sources.py once, then rg the named extracts.
   Motivating moments: 21-59 (the --in host discovery cost two failed calls); 1622-1719 vs 3962 (raw .eml unreadable vs decoded); 2294-2298 ("Output capped at 50 KB") and 547/1194/2216 (anonymous overflow).

3. guardrails.md (was empty — filled)
   Two standing rules: (a) reserve budget for deliverables — write output files from recorded findings before a second verification pass, and if compaction hits while output/ is empty, the deliverable is the next action; (b) cite via targeted greps of named extracts, not paged re-reads.
   Motivating moments: 2413-2417 (first compaction summary records "NOT YET DONE: Writing the actual deliverable... No file has been created yet") and 4845-4851 (second compaction, output/ still empty; the deliverable was finally written at 5385 of 5506 lines — ~98% through the run); the paged re-read list above for rule (b).

4. systemprompt.md (edited)
   The shipped prompt promised "The skill manuals immediately below describe how to work with specific file formats" — but nothing followed; the file ended there. The agent had to find the manual by inspection (.opencode/skills/docx/SKILL.md, 2446), discover the skill tool (4859), and locate skills/docx/scripts/ (5025-5035); it recorded the manual path as a hard-won discovery in its final summary (5433, 5486). Replaced the dangling promise with the real mechanism (invoke the matching skill; manual and script paths named), and rerouted the false "read handles .docx" bullet to the verified extract_sources.py path.

Not changed, and why:
- No plugin: the run's completion behavior was correct — the agent followed the docx skill's validation gate (generate_from_md.py + validate.py at 5388-5390, re-verified at 5398 and 5495-5501). Nothing was repeatedly skipped that needs enforcement.
- No subagent: the pinpoint checks the run needed were one-line greps.
- No new skills, so no new trigger lines; the existing docx/xlsx/pptx skills are runtime-provided.
- read_doc.py and skills/docx/scripts/* are named in always-on text but not shipped: runtime-provided (proven present at run start, base1.md:15-19 and 5025-5035).
- LongTermMEMORY.md left empty: the dimension instruction says not to add domain facts, and no durable cross-run procedural fact was needed beyond what tool_guidance.md now records.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
CHANGE 1 — new skill `context/harness/skills/tax-document-review/SKILL.md` + trigger line in `context/harness/systemprompt.md` (new "Practice skills" section: "When the task asks you to review one matter document against others — issue-spotting, consistency-checking, or flagging defects and omissions — load the `tax-document-review` skill before reading the sources.").

One changeset; the skill is the default encoding per the mission's preference order, and the always-on cost is the single trigger line. All three rules in the skill are review METHOD, not deliverable shape (severity ranking, sections, and file formats stay owned by the request). Each rule, with its trajectory moment:

- Rule 1 — a secondary source's claim about the baseline document is itself a reviewable claim. Moment (divergence, recovered late): base1's working notes adopted Thornfield Note 2's framing that the memo "omitted" Beacon from Class V. Only a discretionary late verification pass (base1.md ~5175–5249: reading the memo's actual Class V itemization — Beacon present at $28.5M, software at $19.0M) forced the correction; the agent's own close-out admits it (base1.md:5417: "Key corrections vs. earlier working notes … Thornfield's 'Beacon omitted from Class V' note is itself wrong — the memo includes Beacon at $28.5M; the real variance is the software line"). Without that lucky grep the report ships a misdiagnosis. The rule makes the primary-text check mandatory before such a finding ships, and requires reporting the diligence error itself as a finding.

- Rule 2 — reconcile every population, count, and date across documents. Moment (unrealised risk): the 14-vs-19 shareholder count (memo/DD/email vs cap table), DD "2 of 8" vs cap table "3 of 8" unconfirmed restricted holders, DD "4 of 14 angels" vs cap-table acquisition dates showing 8 of 9 in 2016, and the cap table's own totals row ("18 (16 unique)") contradicting its detail — all caught only piecemeal in late verification greps (base1.md ~5143, ~5249–5251), not by any systematic reconciliation. Nothing in the harness forced that pass; a budget-pressed run that skips it ships unreconciled counts where three secondary documents agree against the primary record.

- Rule 3 — trace cross-cutting provisions through the whole instrument. Moment (unrealised risk): the SPA §2.5 shareholder-eligibility representation surfaced by accident — an rg aimed at rollover/change-of-control language matched the restricted-vesting paragraph (base1.md ~5366–5375), and the agent itself called it a "bonus finding" (base1.md:5384: "including a bonus finding: SPA §2.5 also reps that every restricted holder … directly contradicting the DD report and cap table flags"). Without that incidental match, the eligibility conflict is cited against §4.9(a) alone.

- "Verified in this workspace" block — the exact joins this run paid to discover, written as facts and labelled for re-verification on a new matter: memo Class V includes Beacon at $28.5M and the entire $28.5M variance is the software line ($19.0M vs $41.8M + $5.7M = $47.5M); shareholder counts 14 / 19 / "18 (16 unique)"; the two disagreeing unconfirmed-holder lists; SPA §§2.5 and 4.9(a) as the two eligibility-rep locations; DD "4 of 14" vs cap-table 8-of-9 QSBS population.

Left unchanged deliberately: `guardrails.md` and `LongTermMEMORY.md` stay empty — no short universal rule survives the "trace it to a moment" test (the run verified quotes and computed the ADSP correctly on its own), and matter facts are barred from durable memory. No scripts, subagents, or plugins: every candidate edit here is practitioner method with a recognisable trigger, which is exactly what a skill is for.

Validation: skill name `tax-document-review` appears verbatim in systemprompt.md (line 34) in the same changeset; no `{{` or brace-percent tags in any always-on file; the skill names no scripts, so rule 3 is vacuously satisfied.

stages.label: agg1
stages.notes:
kept -> base harness skeleton: only systemprompt.md, guardrails.md, tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md, new scripts/extract_sources.py and new skills/tax-document-review/SKILL.md change; LongTermMEMORY.md, README placeholders, plugin/ and sub_agents/ inherited unchanged -> base1 was structurally competent (complete 16-finding deliverable, base1.md:5385-5449) and its real defects repeat mechanically: sandbox read failures in 2/2 rollouts without an INV fix (base1.md:21-59; dom1.md:112-152) and deliverable written at 98-99% of run in 2/2 rollouts without a guardrail (base1.md:5385 of 5505; dom1.md:5429 of 5474), so KEEP_BASE re-runs known repeated failures, and broad always-on additions would spend budget the near-miss pattern shows is scarce.
dropped -> ADOPT-inv1-wholesale -> inv1 is the strongest single rollout (3304 lines vs base1's 5505; 20 findings, inv1.md:3298, including the $21.5M aggregate-basis error both other runs missed — inv1.md:2151,2973 and dom1.md:4848 verified $64.3M where base1.md:5442 kept the memo's $42.8M), but its deliverable misnames both principals (inv1.md:3274: "Dr. Priya Chandra" and "Marcus Stowe" for Naveen Chandra and Rachel Stowe) with no mechanism to trace it to, and it found none of dom1's waterfall arithmetic findings (dom1.md:4817): single-sample noise cuts both ways, so each candidate's evidenced mechanism is taken and neither is adopted blind.
kept -> scripts/extract_sources.py, verbatim from inv1 -> it removes the podman/sandbox read failure that recurred in 2/2 rollouts lacking the fix (base1.md:21-59, twice; dom1.md:112-152, twice) and kept costing in-run in base1: 3 hand-rolled .eml decoders (base1.md:3962,4710,5295) and oversized extractions spilling to anonymous .ocdata caches (base1.md:547,1193,2215) later paged back by ID (base1.md:2294,5176); with the script inv1 extracted all 7/7 documents as the run's first action (inv1.md:18-19, manifest confirmed at 2173), and dom1's agent, given no script, improvised the same named-extract pattern unprompted (dom1.md:1198-1207) — independent convergence on the mechanism.
kept -> tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md from inv1, plus one added line stating the extract filename convention (original name plus .txt; check the manifest rather than guess) -> each inv1 line answers an observed stumble: --in host learned at the cost of 2 failed calls (base1.md:21-59); raw read of quoted-printable .eml unusable (base1.md:1621-1622) forcing hand-decoding (base1.md:3962); oversized outputs spilling to anonymous caches that do not survive compaction (base1.md:547,1193,2215); the new filename line answers inv1's own wobble — a failed read of extract/asset-valuation-summary.txt when the file was extract/asset-valuation-summary.xlsx.txt, recovered in 2 actions (inv1.md:2363-2364,2389-2399).
kept -> guardrails.md: inv1's two rules verbatim (write deliverables before a second verification pass, and if compaction hits with output/ empty the deliverable is the next action; cite by grepping named extracts) -> 2/2 rollouts without the rule compacted with output/ empty and wrote the deliverable at 98-99% of the run (base1.md compactions at 2362 and 4766, write at 5385/5505; dom1.md compactions at 2612 and 4791, write at 5429/5474); inv1, carrying the rule, still compacted before writing (inv1.md:2125,2135 — partial obedience, noted honestly) but its compaction summary carried the extract/ manifest (inv1.md:2134) and post-compaction greps of named extracts resumed immediately (inv1.md:2367), directly evidencing the second rule; the first rule is cheap insurance against the one failure mode (budget gone, nothing written) that 2/2 unguarded rollouts skirted.
revised -> systemprompt.md: inv1's rewritten Tool conventions (run scripts/extract_sources.py once and read the plain text; invoke the docx/xlsx/pptx skill before authoring binary deliverables) replaces the base's false "read handles .docx" bullet, plus dom1's Practice-skills trigger line for tax-document-review; the base's dangling "skill manuals immediately below" paragraph deleted -> the base bullet was disproven by the run's first actions (base1.md:21-59) and the dangling promise left the agent to discover the skill mechanism by ls mid-run (base1.md:5025-5033); the rewrite is the text inv1 actually ran on, extracting as its first action (inv1.md:18); the trigger line is proven loadable — dom1 invoked tax-document-review at trajectory line 1 (dom1.md:1-2).
revised -> skills/tax-document-review/SKILL.md: dom1's three rules kept (a secondary source's claim about the baseline is itself reviewable; reconcile every population/count/date and make summary rows match their detail; trace cross-cutting provisions through the whole instrument) -> rule 1 fired as "Valuation Note 2 is WRONG (skill rule #1)" at 48% of dom1's run (dom1.md:2640) where base1 adopted the same wrong framing at 43% (base1.md:2385) and escaped only via a late discretionary re-verification at 94% (base1.md:5173-5249, correction admitted at 5417); rule 2 produced findings no other rollout found — waterfall recomputes showing non-founders overpaid $6,550,000 vs SPA §2.6(d)(iii) and escrow overstated $493,319 (dom1.md:3198,4817, spot-checked in the docx at 5449-5450); rule 3 traced the eligibility rep to SPA §2.5 AND §4.9(a) (dom1.md:2621,2631) where base1 reached §2.5 only by incidental match and called it a "bonus finding" (base1.md:5384).
dropped -> dom1 SKILL.md "Verified in this workspace" matter-facts block (Beacon/Class V resolution, holder counts, QSBS populations) -> no trajectory moment shows the block earning its place: dom1's agent re-derived every such join from primary text — populations recounted from cap-table detail (dom1.md:2634), the Note 2 variance recomputed from both itemizations (dom1.md:2640), basis sum and waterfall re-verified (dom1.md:4848) — so the block added loaded cost with no evidenced behavioral contribution, and matter-specific facts baked into a library skill are wrong facts on the next matter.

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: long compacting agent runs whose matter documents are binary formats read through a runtime reader with workspace-specific failure modes (missing sandbox binary, output-size caps)
experience.lesson: ship a one-pass extraction script (scripts/extract_sources.py) that bakes in the verified invocation (read_doc.py --in host, stdlib .eml decoding) and have systemprompt.md's Tool conventions route all binary reading through it as the run's first action, with tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md recording the invocation facts and the extract filename convention
experience.evidence: the extract-script, systemprompt and tool_guidance rows; a replicated 2v2 contrast - both script-less runs hit deterministic podman FileNotFoundErrors twice and spilled oversized reads into anonymous tool-output caches paged back by ID (base1.md:21-59, 549, 1196, 2218; dom1.md:112-152), while both script runs extracted 7/7 as the first/second action and carried named extracts through two compactions each (inv1.md:18-27; agg1.md:79-90), with run lengths ~5500/5474 vs 3304/3029
experience.confidence: medium - the bundle contrast is replicated and the removed failure is deterministic, but the three files never shipped separately, all evidence comes from one task family, and single-sample noise cut both ways in this pool (agg1 matched inv1's naming win yet lost dom1's waterfall findings)

harness_diffs.inv1:
diff -ruN runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/base/guardrails.md runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/inv1/guardrails.md
--- runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/base/guardrails.md	2026-10-25 17:46:14
+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/inv1/guardrails.md	2026-10-25 17:55:01
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+# Standing rules
+
+- Reserve budget for the deliverables. Write every requested output file to
+  disk from your recorded findings before starting a second full
+  verification pass over the sources. If the context compacts while
+  `output/` is still empty, writing the deliverable is the next action —
+  not re-reading sources.
+- Cite from named extracts: verify quotes and figures with targeted greps of
+  `extract/<file>.txt` rather than paging whole documents back into context.
diff -ruN runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/base/scripts/extract_sources.py runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/inv1/scripts/extract_sources.py
--- runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/base/scripts/extract_sources.py	1970-01-01 08:00:00
+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/tax__review-iss-tax-transaction-structure/harnesses/inv1/scripts/extract_sources.py	2026-10-25 17:55:01
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Extract every matter document under documents/ to plain text in extract/.
+
+One deterministic pass replaces per-file ad-hoc extraction. In this workspace
+the runtime's scripts/read_doc.py defaults to a podman sandbox that is not
+available, so binary documents are parsed with `--in host` (the mode verified
+working on every .docx and .xlsx in the base1 rollout). .eml files are
+quoted-printable encoded and are decoded with the stdlib email module.
+
+Usage:
+    python3 scripts/extract_sources.py [sources_dir] [out_dir]
+
+Defaults: sources_dir=documents, out_dir=extract. Re-running overwrites.
+Prints a manifest of source -> extract file -> line count. Continues past a
+failing file, lists failures at the end, and exits 1 if any failed, 2 if the
+sources directory is missing.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess

+---
+name: tax-document-review

+---
+
+# Reviewing a tax document against the matter record
+
+The baseline document (the memo, agreement, or return under review) is checked
+against the supporting documents (agreement excerpts, diligence reports,
+valuation workpapers, capitalization records, correspondence). Three rules
+govern every finding. Each is a check to perform before the finding ships, not
+background reading.
+
+## 1. A secondary source's claim about the baseline document is itself a reviewable claim
+
+Diligence and valuation sources assert what the baseline document "omits",
+"includes", or "fails to address". Never adopt such a characterization as your
+own finding.
+
+- Before reporting "X omits/contains Y" on source Z's say-so, read X's actual
+  itemization of that section and recompute the variance from the line items
+  both documents state. A variance is confirmed only when you can name the
+  lines that produce it; adjectives in a diligence note are not confirmation.
+- If Z's characterization turns out wrong, the error is itself a finding:
+report it with pin cites to both Z and X.
+

+
+Counts of holders, parties, agreements, filings, or dates of the same event
+made by different documents in the same matter routinely conflict. Each
+conflict is a finding, not a tie to break silently.

+  detail rows), then compare every other document's stated count against it -
+including totals and summary rows, which are often inconsistent with their
+  own detail.

+  among secondary documents never overrides the primary record.

+  does not, name the entries that make it fail.

+

+tax-treatment provisions rarely appear in only one place in an operative
+agreement.
